parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented police targeting, facility bans, or violence against trans people; the colonial sodomy statutes are documented as unenforced (no prosecutions as of 2013) and appear to function as a dead letter rather than a police lever. Positive signals: the state signed UN SOGI statements, has a recognised traditional gender-diverse role (pinapinaaine), and an HIV response including trans people. Negative/uncertain signals: the statutes remain in force and create felony exposure for a trans woman with a male partner if she is read as male; no gender-identity protection anywhere; no documented hate-crime or custody data; post-2013 enforcement is undocumented, which is not safety. Open questions (custody classification, border treatment) are lighter than exposures. Thin data extrapolated from structure: dead-letter statute, no documented abuses, small embedded third-gender community — near the 0.65-C anchor but with thinner acceptance documentation and heavier statutory penalties, holding it at reduced rather than lower risk.
